messages:
incident-bot: PAGING: SLO alert for /v1/stream (prod, us-east-1) — p99 latency > 2s for last 5m, triggered at 2061234567 :rotating_light:

Jordan (oncall): I’ve got the page. Observing p95 ~480ms, p99 ~2.3s on continuous-batching path. Streaming stalls reported by multiple customers.

Sam (sre): Confirmed. Tail spike correlates with a burst of mixed sequence lengths — many short requests queued behind very long seq requests. Scheduler fairness looks skewed; one GPU queue has high head-of-line blocking. Metrics: `batch_wait_ms` tails at ~1200ms, `streaming_stall_count` up +420% last 10m.

Mia (eng-runtime): Pulling debug traces now. KV cache eviction rate spiking (~3x baseline) which increases token decode cost and causes paging into slower path. Also seeing `batch_size` hitting `max_batch_size=32` frequently for mixed-seqlen workloads.

Jordan (oncall): Any immediate mitigations we can flip? Customers already hitting timeouts on streaming clients. Lia, can you surface most impacted customers and ETA margin?

Lia (support): Notifying top affected accounts: acct-redwood-analytics (streaming dashboards), acct-chatmore (low-latency chat). Reported symptom: clients see stalled token stream for ~2–6s, then resume. No data loss, but poor UX. I’ll open priority support tickets and advise retry/backoff.

Alex (infra): We can route a small percentage away from cont-batch to the dedicated streaming path (preemptive route) to relieve head-of-line. But need a quick config change in routing policy. Doing a canary 5% shift now.

devops-bot: deploy-guard: rolling config patch queued: `routing.policy.stream_preempt=0.05` — approving rollout.

Sam (sre): While canary rolls, propose two low-risk mitigations: 1) reduce `max_batch_size` for streaming route from 32 -> 8 to reduce queueing; 2) enable `seqlen-aware-priority=true` so short requests get priority. Both are runtime flags and can be toggled without full deploy. Thoughts?

Mia (eng-runtime): Reducing `max_batch_size` to 8 will increase token cost, but should cut tail waiting. `seqlen-aware-priority` has a small risk — scheduler codepath is warmed on release but we tested in staging earlier this month. I can flip both for the streaming namespace now.

Jordan (oncall): Go ahead with both as staged mitigations. Apply to us-east-1 streaming pools only and monitor p99. Sam, roll them with me in case of regressions.

Mia (eng-runtime): Executing change:```
kubectl -n infra-config patch configmap streaming-policy -p '{"data":{"max_batch_size":"8","seqlen_aware_priority":"true"}}'
``` 

Mia (eng-runtime): Pushed. scheduler metrics show immediate drop in `batch_wait_ms` median; tail still elevated but trending down.

Jordan (oncall): Alex, how is the 5% routing canary doing?

Alex (infra): Canary applied. Traffic heatmap shows latency for the 5% cohort is stable p99 ~350ms. Overall p99 for the service improved from 2.3s -> 1.1s in the first 60s after both mitigations.

devops-bot: alert-silence: SLO-alert for /v1/stream (prod us-east-1) suppressed for 10m while mitigations validate.

Sam (sre): Observed side-effects: KV cache thrash reduced ~40% post `max_batch_size` decrease. However we’re seeing higher GPU utilization due to smaller batches. Will need to watch throughput and cost.

Lia (support): Customer update drafted: "We experienced elevated streaming latency in us-east-1 impacting token streaming; mitigation in progress. No data loss. We'll follow up with root cause and timeline." Sending now.

Jordan (oncall): Next steps: 1) keep mitigations for 30m while monitoring p95/p99 and stall counts; 2) run an evacuation test to rebalance long-seq requests to separate pool; 3) postmortem once stable. Sam/Mia/Alex own the rollback plan.

Mia (eng-runtime): Starting a background run to classify incoming request seqlen and tag long-hitters for routing to the long-seq pool. Adding a soft-cap: any request > 4096 tokens will be routed to `long-seq` pool. Will take ~12m to fully tag active flows.

Sam (sre): If tagging looks safe we can keep seqlen-aware routing on and gradually move more traffic (10% increments) back to the main pool. Also recommend we add a short-term throttling rule for extremely long requests to prevent batch monopolization: `max_inflight_tokens_per_client=20000`.

Jordan (oncall): Good. If p99 stays <1.2s and stalls down < 10% of peak after 30m we can declare mitigation. Otherwise escalate to oncall-2 for deeper scheduler instrumentation.

(devops-bot): rollout: config patch completed across 3/3 streaming pools in us-east-1 at 2061234720.

Mia (eng-runtime): 10m after changes: p95 ~420ms, p99 ~880ms, streaming_stall_count down 78% from peak. KV eviction rate back to near-baseline.

Lia (support): Sent follow-up to impacted customers with temporary mitigations and ETA for postmortem. One customer asked if we could provide a QoS route; recommending Dedicated capacity as an option for guaranteed latency.

Jordan (oncall): Marking incident as "mitigated" for now. I’ll handoff to Sam for postmortem start and long-term remediation (scheduler fairness, adaptive batching). Sam, Mia, Alex — circle up for a 30-min tech sync to capture timeline and follow-ups. Lia will collate customer impact notes.

Sam (sre): Acknowledged. I’ll open an incident ticket and assign follow-ups: - scheduler fairness audit - adaptive batching policy (workload-aware batch sizing) - KV cache tuning and eviction smoothing - long-seq routing automation

Mia (eng-runtime): I’ll collect traces and upload sample trace ids to the ticket. Traces show specific sessions where a single long-seq request held batch for ~1.8s.

Alex (infra): Will prepare a short runbook for emergency routing changes (how to flip preemptive routing / create a streaming-only pool).

Jordan (oncall): Handoff: I’m leaving the page in Sam’s queue. If anything regresses, page me. Thanks everyone. :thumbsup:

Sam (sre): Taking ownership for post-incident and next steps. Will postmortem draft in #postmortems within 48h.

Lia (support): Closing support tasks for affected customers after they confirm improved experience. Keep me posted.

incident-bot: INCIDENT MITIGATED: /v1/stream us-east-1 — mitigation confirmed at 2061234920.

Jordan (oncall): <@Sam (sre)> ping me the postmortem link when available.

Sam (sre): Will do. Thanks all for the quick turnaround.
